On desktop, the menu is visible by default (without this class) while the menu button is hidden, but the component sets aria-expanded=true on the hidden button and aria-hidden=true on the visible menu.",
  "repair_strategy": "In the init method, detect whether the menu button is rendered (mobile) or hidden (desktop) using offsetParent. Compute menu visibility and button expanded state separately: menu is visible on desktop or when open on mobile; button is expanded only on mobile when menu is open. Set aria-expanded on button and aria-hidden on menu accordingly.",

      "path": "src/govuk/components/header/header.js",
      "sha256": "33e331b7a1f44087522e90d1e295dbc0f915c8b8a82e8afd57a794d21fff4424",
      "before": "Header.prototype.init = function () {\n  if (!this.$module || !this.$menuButton || !this.$menu) {\n    return\n  }\n\n  this.syncState(this.$menu.classList.contains('govuk-header__navigation--open'))\n  this.$menuButton.addEventListener('click', this.handleMenuButtonClick.bind(this))\n}",
      "after": "Header.prototype.init = function () {\n  if (!this.$module || !this.$menuButton || !this.$menu) {\n    return\n  }\n\n  var isMobile = !!this.$menuButton.offsetParent\n  var menuOpen = this.$menu.classList.contains('govuk-header__navigation--open')\n  var menuVisible = !isMobile || menuOpen\n  var buttonExpanded = isMobile && menuOpen\n\n  this.$menuButton.classList.toggle('govuk-header__menu-button--open', buttonExpanded)\n  this.$menuButton.setAttribute('aria-expanded', buttonExpanded)\n  this.$menu.setAttribute('aria-hidden', !menuVisible)\n\n  this.$menuButton.addEventListener('click', this.handleMenuButtonClick.bind(this))\n}"

  ],
  "verification_requirements": [
    "On desktop width, verify that the navigation menu has aria-hidden=\"false\" and the menu button has aria-expanded=\"false\".",
    "On mobile width, verify that clicking the menu button toggles the open class, aria-expanded, and aria-hidden appropriately.",
    "Confirm that Tab navigation reaches the #nav-apply element with role=\"link\" and name=\"Apply\" in both viewport states.",

reasoning:
The issue is that on desktop width, the menu button is hidden (display: none) but the header component incorrectly sets aria-expanded="true" and aria-hidden="false" on the navigation menu. Looking at the code:

In header.js, the init method calls:
```javascript
this.syncState(this.$menu.classList.contains('govuk-header__navigation--open'))
```

On desktop, the menu doesn't have the 'govuk-header__navigation--open' class, so this should be false. But the observed failure shows aria-expanded="true" observed.

Wait, let me look at the CSS again. In the media query for max-width: 40.0525em (mobile):
- .govuk-header__menu-button { display: inline-block }
- .js-enabled .govuk-header__navigation { display: none }
- .js-enabled .govuk-header__navigation--open { display: block }

On desktop (wider than 40.0525em):
- .govuk-header__menu-button { display: none }
- .govuk-header__navigation { display: block (default) }

So on desktop, the menu is visible by default (no --open class needed), and the menu button is hidden.

The problem is in the init method. It checks for the --open class, but on desktop the menu is visible WITHOUT that class. So isVisible should be true on desktop (menu visible), false on mobile (menu hidden unless --open).

But the syncState sets:
- aria-expanded on button = isVisible
- aria-hidden on menu = !isVisible

On desktop: menu visible, button hidden. So aria-expanded should be false (button not expanded), aria-hidden should be false (menu not hidden).

On mobile: menu hidden by default, button visible. So aria-expanded should be false (button not expanded), aria-hidden should be true (menu hidden).

When menu opens on mobile: aria-expanded true, aria-hidden false.

The current code checks for --open class only. On desktop, --open class is not present, so isVisible = false, which sets aria-expanded=false (correct) but aria-hidden=true (WRONG - menu is visible on desktop).

The fix: determine visibility based on whether the menu button is hidden (desktop) or the --open class (mobile).

The previous attempt tried to use offsetParent but that didn't work. Let me think of a better approach.

We can check if the menu button is visible (display !== 'none') to determine if we're in mobile mode. If button is hidden -> desktop -> menu visible. If button visible -> mobile -> menu visibility depends on --open class.

Actually, simpler: the menu is visible if either:
1. The menu button is hidden (desktop), OR
2. The menu has the --open class (mobile open)

So: isVisible = !this.$menuButton.offsetParent || this.$menu.classList.contains('govuk-header__navigation--open')

Wait, offsetParent is null when element is not rendered (display: none). But the previous attempt used this and it failed.

Let me check the previous attempt's edit:
```javascript
const isVisible = !this.$menuButton.offsetParent || this.$menu.classList.contains('govuk-header__navigation--open')
this.syncState(isVisible)
```

But the failure still shows aria-expanded="true" observed. That suggests isVisible evaluated to true.

On desktop, menu button has display: none, so offsetParent should be null, so !this.$menuButton.offsetParent = true, so isVisible = true. That would set aria-expanded=true on the button, which is wrong because the button is hidden on desktop.

Ah! The issue: on desktop, the menu IS visible, but the button is NOT expanded (it's hidden). So aria-expanded should be false on the button, but aria-hidden should be false on the menu.

The syncState function sets BOTH based on the same isVisible:
- button.aria-expanded = isVisible
- menu.aria-hidden = !isVisible

But on desktop: menu visible (aria-hidden=false), button hidden (aria-expanded=false). These are the SAME value (both false).

On mobile closed: menu hidden (aria-hidden=true), button not expanded (aria-expanded=false). These are DIFFERENT.

On mobile open: menu visible (aria-hidden=false), button expanded (aria-expanded=true). These are DIFFERENT.

So the single isVisible boolean cannot represent both states correctly for all cases.

We need to separate the concerns:
- Menu visibility (for aria-hidden on menu)
- Button expanded state (for aria-expanded on button)

On desktop: menu visible, button not expanded (hidden)
On mobile closed: menu hidden, button not expanded
On mobile open: menu visible, button expanded

So:
- menuAriaHidden = !menuVisible
- buttonAriaExpanded = buttonVisible && menuVisible (only expanded when button visible AND menu open)

Actually, buttonAriaExpanded should be true only when the button is visible AND the menu is open (--open class).

Menu visible = button hidden (desktop) OR (button visible AND --open class)

Let me rewrite syncState to take two parameters, or compute them separately.

But the syncState is called from handleMenuButtonClick with isVisible = toggle result (which is the --open class state after toggle). On mobile, that works. On desktop, the button isn't clickable (hidden), so handleMenuButtonClick never fires.

The issue is only in init().

In init(), we need to set initial state correctly.

On desktop: 
- menuVisible = true
- buttonExpanded = false

On mobile:
- menuVisible = this.$menu.classList.contains('govuk-header__navigation--open')
- buttonExpanded = menuVisible

So in init():
```javascript
var isMobile = !!this.$menuButton.offsetParent; // button rendered
var menuVisible = !isMobile || this.$menu.classList.contains('govuk-header__navigation--open');
var buttonExpanded = isMobile && menuVisible;

this.$menuButton.classList.toggle('govuk-header__menu-button--open', buttonExpanded);
this.$menuButton.setAttribute('aria-expanded', buttonExpanded);
this.$menu.setAttribute('aria-hidden', !menuVisible);
```

But we need to keep syncState for the click handler. The click handler only runs on mobile (button visible), so there isVisible = menuVisible = buttonExpanded.

So we can either:
1. Modify syncState to accept two parameters, or
2. Compute separately in init and keep syncState as is for click handler (since on mobile they're the same)

Option 2 is simpler. In init, compute both and set attributes directly. In handleMenuButtonClick, the existing syncState works because on mobile, menuVisible === buttonExpanded.

Let me write the fix.

The current init:
```javascript
Header.prototype.init = function () {
  if (!this.$module || !this.$menuButton || !this.$menu) {
    return
  }

  this.syncState(this.$menu.classList.contains('govuk-header__navigation--open'))
  this.$menuButton.addEventListener('click', this.handleMenuButtonClick.bind(this))
}
```

Change to:
```javascript
Header.prototype.init = function () {
  if (!this.$module || !this.$menuButton || !this.$menu) {
    return
  }

  var isMobile = !!this.$menuButton.offsetParent
  var menuOpen = this.$menu.classList.contains('govuk-header__navigation--open')
  var menuVisible = !isMobile || menuOpen
  var buttonExpanded = isMobile && menuOpen

  this.$menuButton.classList.toggle('govuk-header__menu-button--open', buttonExpanded)
  this.$menuButton.setAttribute('aria-expanded', buttonExpanded)
  this.$menu.setAttribute('aria-hidden', !menuVisible)

  this.$menuButton.addEventListener('click', this.handleMenuButtonClick.bind(this))
}
```

This should fix the desktop case: isMobile=false, menuOpen=false, menuVisible=true, buttonExpanded=false. So aria-expanded=false, aria-hidden=false. Correct.

On mobile closed: isMobile=true, menuOpen=false, menuVisible=false, buttonExpanded=false. aria-expanded=false, aria-hidden=true. Correct.

On mobile open: isMobile=true, menuOpen=true, menuVisible=true, buttonExpanded=true. aria-expanded=true, aria-hidden=false. Correct.

And handleMenuButtonClick still works because it toggles menuOpen and calls syncState(menuOpen), which on mobile sets both to menuOpen (since isMobile=true).

Now, the previous attempt used a similar approach but with offsetParent check in a different way. Let me check why it failed.

Previous attempt:
```javascript
const isVisible = !this.$menuButton.offsetParent || this.$menu.classList.contains('govuk-header__navigation--open')
this.syncState(isVisible)
```

This sets both aria-expanded and aria-hidden based on isVisible. On desktop: !offsetParent = true, so isVisible=true. Then aria-expanded=true (wrong), aria-hidden=false (correct for menu). So the button gets aria-expanded=true even though it's hidden.

My new fix separates the two.

Root cause: The header component incorrectly determines initial menu visibility by only checking for the 'govuk-header__navigation--open' class. On desktop, the menu is visible by default (without this class) while the menu button is hidden, but the component sets aria-expanded=true on the hidden button and aria-hidden=true on the visible menu.

Repair strategy: In the init method, detect whether the menu button is rendered (mobile) or hidden (desktop) using offsetParent. Compute menu visibility and button expanded state separately: menu is visible on desktop or when open on mobile; button is expanded only on mobile when menu is open. Set aria-expanded on button and aria-hidden on menu accordingly.

Expected accessibility effect: On desktop, the navigation menu will have aria-hidden="false" and the menu button will have aria-expanded="false", exposing the navigation links to assistive technology. On mobile, the menu button will correctly reflect the menu state.

Functional risks: 
- If the menu button's display property changes for reasons other than viewport width, visibility detection may be incorrect.
- Future CSS changes affecting the button's layout could break the offsetParent check.
- The component relies on the 'govuk-header__navigation--open' class for mobile menu state; ensuring that class toggling remains correct is essential.

Verification requirements:
- On desktop width, verify that the navigation menu has aria-hidden="false" and the menu button has aria-expanded="false".
- On mobile width, verify that clicking the menu button toggles the open class, aria-expanded, and aria-hidden appropriately.
- Confirm that Tab navigation reaches the #nav-apply element with role="link" and name="Apply" in both viewport states.
- Ensure that the menu button remains functional for showing/hiding the menu on mobile.
